day_04_morning: ^The memory gardens sit behind Saint Orra's chapel, where the ash cannot reach.
^Every rose has a name written on its tag. Every name has a date.
^Sister Oria moves between the rows with a watering can and a patience older than the Bell.
^You are late, Bellkeeper, she says. You were late the last time too.
^You do not ask how she knows.
^The garden is for what the Bell takes, she says. We keep the names so the city has somewhere to look.
^A small wren lands on the chapel roof. It watches you the way a person would.
^Refuse the blessing. Ask what the garden costs.
kneel: ^Oria touches your brow. Her hand smells of soil and cold tea.
^Remember one name a day, she says. That is all the Bell cannot take.
ask: ^The wren? Oria does not look up. It has been here longer than the garden.
^She waters a rose before she answers. Longer than the name for it.
refuse: ^Every name here was taken from someone, you say. What do you charge them to remember?
^Oria sets down the watering can. Nothing, she says. That is the cost.
day_04_afternoon: ^The Clockwork Saint kneels at the center of the garden, built into the root of the chapel.
^It has been still for a hundred years. Today its eyes are open.
^Do not break it, Oria says. Break the bell heart. It will remember how to sleep.
^The Saint rises. Brass hands unfold like a prayer.
^Somewhere inside it, a small bell begins to ring.
^The roses turn their heads toward the sound.
shield: ^You put yourself in front of Oria. The Saint's shadow falls over both of you.
^It is not the Saint we are fighting, Oria says. It is the thing that wound it.
strike: ^The heart is a knot of gears behind the Saint's ribs. You can see it through the brass.
^Mara sees it too. She plants her feet and waits for your word.
^Break the heart, not the Saint, you say.
day_04_night: ^The wren is waiting on the Spire roof. Up close, it is a girl.
^She is counting under her breath. Eight. Nine. She stops when she sees you.
^You are the Bellkeeper, she says. You look tired for someone who gets to try again.
^My name is Wren. I have been on this roof for four loops.
^The Bell takes most things, she says. It does not take me. I have not decided if that is a gift.
^Ask Wren to come down with you.
come: ^Wren looks at the drop, then at you. She does not take your hand, but she follows.
^One condition, she says. When it gets bad, you do not decide for me.
remember: ^I write it down, she says. Every morning. The same nine things.
^She shows you a slate covered in chalk. Your name is at the top.
leave: ^You leave her counting. On the way down, you hear her start again from one.
^The Bell rings once, quietly, as if it has won something small.
